proof_attempt_summary: The run proved a matched risk and honest expected-length rate for the full stated heterogeneous class through J_n <= floor(n^(2/3)), with an observable count-aware procedure. The original all-J frontier remained unresolved: sparse cells have a one-sided reciprocal lower envelope and the singleton endpoint has bounds with unmatched exponent constants. A guarded reframe around the proved dense theorem passed math review but remained below the field novelty floor at subfield tier.
tldr: The primary contribution is a matched minimax theorem for the exact hard clamp at dose \(1/2\) over the full heterogeneous-density model: uniformly for \(1\leq J_n\leq\lfloor n^{2/3}\rfloor\), both minimax absolute risk and uniformly honest expected length are of order \(n^{-1/3}\).  The explicit fixed-size three-block nearest-neighbor estimator and connected interval attain both upper bounds, use \(1/2\) in empty cells, and retain the unmodified outcome in singleton cells.  The observed and causal decision problems coincide only on the simultaneous bounded-density Lipschitz lifts; broader Díaz-compatible classes inherit only lower converses by inclusion.  Secondary results give a dose-localized reciprocal lower envelope and a named factorial-polynomial endpoint procedure with nonmatching stretched-exponential bounds.  The exact singleton exponent and the multiplicatively matched frontier above \(\lfloor n^{2/3}\rfloor\) remain open, and no minimax elbow is asserted.
gap: Díaz et al. identify the exact minimum-exercise clamp but do not give rates for its nonregular point evaluation. Zeng et al. and Jiao et al. show how sparse labelled cells and factorial approximation create nonlinear functional-estimation frontiers, but their targets have no dose-localization bias. Existing honest-interval theory does not cover a random-occupancy marked reciprocal functional with empty and singleton cells.
fill: The baseline branch uses an explicit uniformly randomized fixed-size split and a count-aware radius, the lower branch fixes the observable clamp mass and retained-course mean while encoding the target in an average reciprocal, and the open multiscale branch couples local smoothing to variance-sensitive reciprocal approximation. A separately defined common-density subclass supplies the \(n^{-1/3}\) sanity benchmark without being used as an upper bound for the heterogeneous-density class. The reciprocal diagnostic is totalized by an explicit occupancy threshold, a zero convention below it, and a feasible fixed-sample width above it. The resulting full-class rate, estimator, and connected interval are required to use one set of constants over dense, intermediate, and singleton regimes.
